title: The procure-to-pay (P2P) process: A step-by-step guide
summary: Learn the nine steps of the procure-to-pay process, where AI can help, and how connected purchasing data makes accruals easier to prepare at month-end.
body_markdown:
Key takeaways


- P2P follows nine steps, from need identification through vendor payment.
- Intake-to-pay adds structured intake and early approvals before the purchase moves downstream.
- Best-in-class teams process invoices in 3.1 days at $2.78 each, according to[Ardent Partners' 2025 research](https://www.datocms-assets.com/80283/1744404602-ardent-partners-ap-metrics-that-matter-in-2025-pagero-final.pdf) .
- Artificial intelligence can help validate requests, code invoices, and resolve exceptions before month-end.
- Accrual Automation uses purchasing records to prepare supported entries for human review when goods or services have been received but remain uninvoiced.
- For the broader accounting implications, read Zip's guide to[building the accounting organization of 2030](https://zip.com/resources/accounting-2030) .


The procure-to-pay (P2P) process moves a purchase from an identified need through supplier payment. When its records stay connected, the process also gives accounting a clearer view of expenses incurred before an invoice arrives.


This connection is important at month-end. An approved purchase order alone cannot prove that an expense belongs in the current period. Accounting needs evidence of what was delivered, what has been invoiced, and what remains outstanding. Modern P2P tools can bring those records together so teams can resolve exceptions earlier and prepare supported accruals without rebuilding the purchase history in a spreadsheet.


The performance gap is substantial. Ardent Partners’ report,[Accounts Payable Metrics That Matter in 2025](https://www.datocms-assets.com/80283/1744404602-ardent-partners-ap-metrics-that-matter-in-2025-pagero-final.pdf) , puts best-in-class invoice processing at **3.1 days and $2.78 per invoice** , with a **49.2% touchless rate** . Those figures describe invoice processing; the same connected data can also help finance close the books.


## What is a procure-to-pay process?


**The procure-to-pay process is the sequence an organization uses to purchase goods and services.** It begins when someone identifies a need and ends when the corresponding invoice is paid. Along the way, the organization approves the request, issues a purchase order (PO), records delivery, and checks the invoice before payment.


Procurement covers the broader work of selecting suppliers and managing commercial relationships; P2P carries an individual purchase through payment. Purchase-to-pay is commonly used as another name for procure-to-pay.


Payment completes the purchasing cycle, but accounting may need to recognize an expense earlier. If a supplier delivers before the period ends and invoices later, finance needs enough evidence to record the expense in the correct period.


## Procure-to-pay vs. intake-to-pay


[Intake-to-pay (I2P)](https://zip.com/solutions/intake-to-pay) connects the initial request with the purchasing cycle, bringing review forward before spend is committed.


Dimension Procure-to-pay Intake-to-pay


Where it starts Purchase need or requisition Initial employee request


Primary focus Ordering through payment Request review through payment


Visibility timing Often formalized at requisition or PO; earlier visibility depends on the design Captures intent before spend is committed


Risk control Purchase authorization and transaction checks Earlier supplier and purchase-risk review


Who uses it Procurement, AP, and receiving teams Requesters and specialist reviewers, alongside procurement and AP


Goal Complete authorized purchases and pay accurately Guide purchases early and retain context through payment


## 9 steps of the procure-to-pay process


The following steps describe the standard P2P cycle. Supplier performance is monitored throughout, even though it appears as a distinct step here.


Step Typical owner Record created Where AI helps


1. Identify need Requester Need statement Suggest relevant purchase context


2. Create requisition Requester Purchase requisition Extract details from supporting documents


3. Approve requisition Budget owner and reviewers Approval record Identify required reviewers


4. Issue PO Procurement Purchase order Check purchase details


5. Confirm receipt Receiving team or service owner Receipt or acceptance record Flag missing confirmations


6. Receive invoice AP Invoice record Extract and validate invoice data


7. Monitor supplier Procurement Performance record Surface recurring discrepancies


8. Approve invoice AP and authorized approver Match and approval record Flag differences for review


9. Pay supplier AP or treasury Payment record Assist with anomaly detection


### 1. Need identification


An employee or department identifies goods or services needed to move work forward. A clear statement of the need helps procurement assess timing, existing suppliers, and the appropriate route to purchase. AI can also surface needs tied to upcoming renewals or changes in supplier performance.


### 2. Requisition creation


The requester creates a[purchase requisition](https://zip.com/blog/purchase-requisition-vs-purchase-order) with the proposed supplier, amount, and delivery details. Supporting documents, such as a quote or statement of work, give reviewers the context they need.[AI-assisted intake](https://zip.com/blog/introducing-ai-automation-p2p) can draw information from those materials and prepare a structured request.


### 3. Requisition approval


The request moves to the people responsible for budget, policy, and any specialist review. Routing the right reviewers at the same time can reduce delays. The approval record also establishes who authorized the purchase and under what conditions.


### 4. Purchase order issuance


Once approved, the requisition becomes a PO sent to the supplier. It records the authorized purchase and its terms. Keeping the PO current as quantities or amounts change is important for invoice matching and later accrual calculations.


A PO can form a binding agreement between buyer and supplier once accepted, subject to the governing terms. For a purchase without a PO, AP must establish authorization and route the invoice to its owner for coding and approval under the company’s exception policy.


### 5. Goods or services receipt


The receiving team confirms what the supplier delivered. A receipt may document the quantity of physical goods, while a service owner may confirm completed work or a contractual milestone. Discrepancies should be resolved against the PO before an invoice is approved.


For services, the business owner or project lead confirms acceptance against the agreed scope. Evidence may include an approved deliverable or sign-off on a completed milestone, with the service date recorded for accounting.


This confirmation also helps accounting determine whether an expense was incurred. An open PO shows a commitment, but it does not, by itself, establish that goods or services were received.


### 6. Invoice receiving


The supplier sends an invoice, which accounts payable (AP) captures and prepares for review. Invoice formats vary, so[AI-powered extraction](https://zip.com/products/procure-to-pay) can help read the document and place its details in a consistent record.


Invoices may arrive by email or through a supplier portal. Electronic data interchange (EDI) and Extensible Markup Language (XML) provide structured submission options. AP needs the invoice number and date, supplier identity, and line items with amounts. Payment terms and the PO number, where applicable, complete the record used for validation.


Timing creates a separate issue. Goods or services received in one accounting period may not be invoiced until the next. When receipt and invoice status are connected, finance can identify that gap before close instead of discovering it while reconciling accounts.


### 7. Supplier performance monitoring


Throughout the cycle, procurement monitors delivery quality and the supplier’s adherence to agreed terms. Transaction records can reveal recurring discrepancies and help teams address them before the next renewal or purchase.


### 8. Invoice approval and three-way match


A three-way match compares the invoice with the PO and the receipt. If the records agree with the organization’s rules, the invoice can move toward approval. Differences require investigation before payment.


Two-way vs. three-way matching


Two-way matching compares the invoice with the PO. Three-way matching also checks the receipt to confirm delivery before payment.


Ardent Partners'[Accounts Payable Metrics That Matter in 2025](https://www.datocms-assets.com/80283/1744404602-ardent-partners-ap-metrics-that-matter-in-2025-pagero-final.pdf) reports a 49.2% touchless invoice processing rate for best-in-class organizations, compared with a 32.6% industry average. These are invoice-processing benchmarks, and consistent purchasing and receiving records help teams reduce matching exceptions.


Connected records make both matching and exception handling more reliable. They also show finance what has been received without a corresponding invoice, which is a common source of period-end accruals.


### 9. Vendor payment


After the invoice is approved, AP pays the supplier according to the agreed terms. An invoice with unresolved differences may be returned for correction.


When an invoice arrives for a previously accrued expense, accounting must address the earlier estimate so the expense is not counted twice. The reversal and any true-up follow the company’s policy and the actual invoice amount.[The controller’s guide to the continuous close](https://zip.com/resources/continuous-close-guide) explores how connected purchasing and accounting records make this work easier to manage throughout the period.


## How P2P connects to month-end accruals


Suppose a team confirms delivery on September 28, but the supplier invoices in October. The September expense may still need to be recognized under the organization’s accounting policy. Finance has to determine the amount from the receipt, PO, contract, or other support, and then prepare an accrual for review.

## Procure-to-pay best practices


A reliable P2P process gives each transaction a consistent path while preserving room for appropriate human judgment.


- **Centralize purchasing records.** Keep requests, POs, receipts, and invoices connected so reviewers can see the history of a transaction.
- **Standardize approval rules.** Define who reviews a purchase and which exceptions require escalation. Apply those rules consistently.
- **Pair automation with AI agents.** Rules can move routine transactions forward, while agents can interpret context and propose a response when a case needs more attention.
- **Measure operational and close outcomes.** Track invoice cycle time and exception rates alongside days to close. Accrual accuracy can show whether purchasing data is helping accounting recognize expenses correctly.
- **Maintain supplier relationships.** Clear communication about orders and discrepancies helps prevent avoidable invoice delays.
- **Design for an audit trail.** Retain the source documents, approvals, and reasons behind decisions, including decisions assisted by AI.
- **Enforce PO-first purchasing.** Require an approved PO before an order is placed, with documented exceptions for permitted categories. Review non-PO invoices monthly to identify repeat sources and address the underlying purchasing behavior.
- **Assign an owner for each exception type.** Send price differences to procurement and missing receipts to the receiving owner. AP should track unresolved cases and escalate them against an agreed deadline.


### How to measure P2P performance


Define each key performance indicator (KPI) consistently and compare results over time. Separate invoice-processing measures from the full purchasing cycle so improvements can be traced to the right stage.


Metric Definition Why it matters


Touchless invoice rate Invoices processed without manual intervention ÷ all processed invoices Shows how often automation completes processing


Cost per invoice Total AP invoice-processing cost ÷ invoices processed Tracks processing efficiency


Requisition-to-pay cycle time Elapsed time from requisition submission to completed payment Exposes delays across the full cycle


Exception rate Invoices requiring exception handling ÷ invoices processed Reveals recurring data or matching problems


Percent of spend with a PO PO-backed spend ÷ addressable purchasing spend Shows compliance with purchase authorization


Receiving compliance Orders with required receipt confirmation ÷ orders requiring confirmation Shows whether acceptance evidence is available


On-time payment rate Invoices paid by their due date ÷ invoices due Tracks payment reliability


Treat accrual readiness as an output of the P2P process. Recording delivery promptly and keeping PO balances accurate gives accounting stronger evidence before close week begins.


## Common procure-to-pay process challenges


### Siloed data and tooling


When requests, receipts, and invoices sit in separate systems, teams spend time reconciling records before they can act. A connected[procurement orchestration platform](https://zip.com/blog/procurement-orchestration) brings transaction context together and makes exceptions easier to investigate.


### Compliance with policies and regulations


For organizations in scope, the[Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX)](https://www.sec.gov/info/accountants/stafficreporting.htm) makes financial reporting controls a priority. Approval evidence and traceable changes support those controls. Supplier records containing personal data also need appropriate protection under the[General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/information-business-and-organisations/principles-gdpr_en) and the[California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA)](https://oag.ca.gov/privacy/ccpa) , where applicable.


‍


Financial-services organizations subject to the[Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA)](https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora) must address technology-provider risk. Teams using AI should assess their obligations under the[European Union (EU) AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai) according to the system’s use and risk classification, then document the required oversight.


### Supplier onboarding and management


Incomplete supplier records can hold up orders and payments. A consistent[supplier onboarding process](https://zip.com/products/supplier-onboarding) collects the required information and gives teams a shared record for ongoing management.


### Spend visibility and analysis


Fragmented purchasing records make it difficult to understand committed spend. Connecting approved requests with POs and invoices helps finance see what has been ordered and what has actually been billed.


### Long approval cycle times


Requests stall when reviewers receive them one after another or lack enough context to decide. Parallel routing and clear escalation rules can move routine requests forward while preserving review for exceptions.


Zip reports that[27% of respondents in its research](https://zip.com/blog/procurement-orchestration) require 10 or more approvals for a single purchase. Route independent reviews in parallel, while preserving dependencies that require one decision before another can begin.


### Unclear exception ownership


A price mismatch can stall when procurement expects AP to resolve it and AP is waiting for the requester. Assign an owner by exception type and keep a visible queue with escalation deadlines, so each discrepancy has a clear next action.


### Manual accrual reconstruction at period-end


Accounting often has to search for received-but-uninvoiced purchases during the close.[Accrual Automation](https://zip.com/blog/accrual-automation) can use the PO, receipt, and invoice status to prepare a supported estimate for approval. Finance still reviews the accounting treatment and any missing evidence.


## 6 ways a modern P2P platforms transforms procurement


### 1. Standardizes the purchasing process


A shared platform applies approval rules and records exceptions consistently. Employees get a clearer path to purchase, and finance receives more dependable transaction data.


### 2. Enhances visibility and analysis


Teams can follow a purchase from request through payment and see where it stalls. The same view helps accounting identify delivered items that have yet to be invoiced.


### 3. Manages documents in context


Quotes, POs, receipts, and invoices remain attached to the relevant transaction. Reviewers can inspect the supporting record without searching across inboxes.


### 4. Improves supplier onboarding


A central supplier record helps procurement coordinate required checks before purchasing begins. It also gives AP dependable details when invoices and payments arrive.


### 5. Connects with the finance stack


A P2P platform can share approved transaction data with the existing enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. That connection helps accounting use current purchasing information without replacing its system of record.


### 6. Brings AI into procurement and accounting work


AI can assist with intake, invoice coding, and exception resolution using information captured upstream. Zip’s[AI Automation for P2P](https://zip.com/blog/introducing-ai-automation-p2p) extends that context across the purchasing cycle.


Accrual Automation brings the same purchasing context to period-end accounting. Its calculation engine prepares proposed entries from the underlying records, while AI follows up for missing information. Human approval and a traceable calculation remain part of the process. This is one practical step toward the[continuous close](https://zip.com/blog/continuous-close-playbook) , where teams address accounting issues as they arise.


## What to look for in P2P software


Use these questions to test how a platform will support your purchasing process and existing controls.


‍


- **Guided intake.** How does the system collect the right information for each purchase category?
- **Parallel approval routing.** Can independent reviews run together while required dependencies remain enforced?
- **Automated three-way match.** How are tolerances configured and discrepancies routed to an owner?
- **Enterprise resource planning (ERP) sync.** Which records sync, and how are failures or duplicate postings handled?
- **AI invoice coding.** How can AP review a suggested code and understand the evidence behind it?
- **Supplier portal.** Can suppliers submit invoices and check status without contacting AP?
- **Audit trail.** Can you trace approvals and changes back to the responsible person?
- **Reporting and KPIs.** Can you calculate our agreed measures and inspect the underlying transactions?

## Where to start modernizing your procure-to-pay process


Start by finding where transactions lose context. If invoices regularly arrive without usable PO or receipt information, improve those handoffs first. If approvals are the main bottleneck, review routing rules and the information requesters provide.


Finance can also examine accrual visibility as an early measure of progress. Compare the list of open POs with confirmed receipts and invoice status. Identify which items still require manual follow-up at period-end and whether the supporting records are available for review.


Modernization can build on an existing ERP. Zip’s[procure-to-pay solution](https://zip.com/products/procure-to-pay) connects purchasing and AP activity while syncing approved transactions with finance systems.


## Frequently asked questions about the procure-to-pay process


### What is the procure-to-pay process?


Procure-to-pay is the process an organization uses to request, approve, order, and receive goods or services, then process the invoice and pay the supplier. It connects purchasing decisions with the records AP needs to approve payment.


### What are the steps in the procure-to-pay cycle?


The nine steps are need identification, requisition creation, requisition approval, PO issuance, goods or services receipt, invoice receiving, supplier performance monitoring, invoice approval, and vendor payment. Supplier monitoring continues throughout the cycle.


### What is the difference between procure-to-pay and intake-to-pay?


P2P manages the purchase through payment. I2P starts earlier by capturing and assessing the initial request before a PO is created. Organizations may use both as parts of one connected process.


### What is a three-way match in P2P?


A three-way match compares the supplier invoice with the PO and the record of goods or services received. It helps AP identify differences before approving payment.


### How is AI changing the procure-to-pay process?


AI can structure purchase requests, assist with invoice coding, and surface exceptions using information from earlier stages. Teams can set rules for which actions proceed and which require human review.
